attacks.claim: Description length is unbounded, and TRAILING_PUNCT is quadratic on long punctuation runs inside a URL. A single owner-written URL with a long dot run followed by a non-punctuation character can freeze the item page for every neighbor who views it, and expanded mode renders one DOM node per token with no cap.
attacks.evidence: const TRAILING_PUNCT = /[.,;:!?)\]]+$/; ... ABSENT: any max-length check on item.description before tokenize/ItemDescription; expanded path renders all tokens

attacks.claim: A leading link longer than the limit is pushed whole, so the collapsed view is not shortened. A pasted long URL at the start of a description defeats the collapse, leaving the Request to borrow button screens down on phones, which is the PR's stated motivation.
attacks.evidence: } else if (out.length === 0) { out.push(t); // a leading link is shown whole rather than collapsing to nothing

attacks.claim: Long unbroken URLs have no wrap rule. The diff adds no overflow-wrap or word-break for the link or .item-description__body, and the existing body style only sets white-space: pre-line, so a long URL can overflow a narrow phone viewport.
attacks.evidence: {t.value} ... ABSENT: overflow-wrap/word-break for .item-description__body or links

attacks.claim: The hard-cut branch splits a whitespace-free text token mid-word, which conflicts with the PR's general 'whitespace or token boundary' description. The test title 'truncation never splits a link or a word' asserts exactly that word split. URLs are never split, so the URL guarantee holds, but the title and description are misleading.

Owner-authored http(s) links become clickable for every signed-in neighbor and open in a new tab, with no domain warning or interstitial. This widens the phishing and malware surface inside the app. The protocol check is the only gate.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: domain allowlist, warning, or interstitial; target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"

attacks.claim: Tests do not cover the pathological cases: a leading link longer than the limit, an unbroken long URL, or a long trailing-punctuation run. The collapse test also never asserts that collapsed text is shorter than the limit or ends at a word boundary.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: tests for leading link > limit, unbroken long URL, or long punctuation run; expect(screen.queryByRole('link')).toBeNull(); with no check on collapsed text length

attacks.claim: The toggle sets aria-expanded and also changes its label between 'Show more' and 'Show less', so screen readers may announce the state twice. A stable label with aria-expanded is the usual pattern.
Each link's accessible name is the raw URL, which screen readers read character by character and which is hard to scan. The link also opens a new window with no announcement.
attacks.evidence: {t.value} where t.value is the raw matched URL; target="_blank"

attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT strips a closing ')' even when it is balanced inside the URL, so parenthesized paths such as wiki links get a truncated href that points to a broken address. The displayed text and href can also differ.
expanded is component state with no key or reset. If the same instance renders a different item's text, the previous item's expanded state carries over.
attacks.evidence: export function ItemDescription({ text, limit = 280 }: ...) { const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);

attacks.claim: The budget is counted in UTF-16 code units in the main loop but in code points in the hard-cut branch. For astral characters such as emoji, the hard cut can exceed the intended limit in UTF-16 units, and no test covers this.

When a long unbroken token follows a few words, the cut falls back to the last whitespace, so the collapsed text can shrink to almost nothing (for example 'Hi…'). The out.length===0 fallback covers only a token that comes first.
